chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When you are seated in the state of ablution and do not know whether you washed your forearm or not, then repeat upon it, and upon all that you doubted that you did not wash or wipe, from what Allah has specified, as long as you are in the state of ablution. So when you rise from the ablution and are finished, you have entered another state, in prayer or other than prayer, and you doubt in part of what Allah has specified from what Allah the Exalted has obligated upon you regarding ablution, then there is nothing upon you.

And if you doubt regarding wiping your head, and moisture hits your beard, then wipe with it upon it and upon the back of your feet; and if moisture does not hit, then the ablution is not broken by the doubt, and proceed in your prayer. And if you are certain that you did not complete your ablution, then repeat upon what you left with certainty until you complete the ablution.

Hammad said, and Hariz said, and Zurara said: I said to him, 'A man left part of his forearm or part of his body in the major ablution (ghusl).' He said: 'If he doubts, then there is moisture with him and he is in his prayer, he wipes with it upon it; and if he is certain, he returns and repeats the water upon it as long as moisture does not hit. If doubt enters him and he has entered another state, let him proceed in his prayer and there is nothing upon him. And if it becomes apparent, he returns and repeats the water upon it. And if he sees it and there is moisture with him, he wipes upon it and repeats the prayer with certainty. And if he is doubting, there is nothing upon him regarding his doubt, so let him proceed in his prayer.'

key_terms.غُسْلِ الْجَنَابَةِ: Major ablution (ritual washing for major impurity)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on doubt in washing during ablution or prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'al-istishab' (presumption of continuity) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between doubt during the act of wudu versus after its completion. It clarifies that minor uncertainty in washing or wiping does not invalidate purity unless accompanied by certainty of omission, a nuance particularly highlighted in the context of ghusl by scholars like al-Kulayni. The ruling ensures that worshippers are not burdened by excessive doubt, allowing them to proceed with prayer unless they are certain a required component was missed.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Zurara, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws having said: ‘When you are seated upon an Ablution (Wudhu) and do not know whether you have washed your forearm or not, so repeat upon it, and upon the entirety of whatever you have doubted in. So, that you have not washed it nor wiped it (contrary to) what Allahazwj has Specified, for as long as you are in the state of the Ablution (Wudhu).

So when you arise from the Ablution (Wudhu) and are free, so you have come to be in another state regarding Salaat or other than Salaat, and you doubt in part of what Allahazwj has Specified from what Allahazwj the Exalted has Obligated upon you with regards to an Ablution (Wudhu), so there is nothing upon you.

And if you doubt regarding wiping of your head, and a residue hits your beard, so wipe with it over it, and upon the back of your feet; and if a residue does not hit, so there is not breakage of the Ablution (Wudhu) with the doubt, and go to your Salaat. And if you are certain that you did not complete your Ablution (Wudhu), so repeat upon whatever you neglected with a certainty until you come to be upon the Ablution (Wudhu)’.

Hammad said, and Hareyz said, and Zurara said, ‘I said to himasws, ‘A man neglects part of his forearm, or part of his body in the major Ablution (Wudhu) (for the sexual impurity)’. So heasws said: ‘When he doubts, then he was with residue (of water), and he was in his Salaat, he should wipe with it upon it; and if it was a certainty, he should return and repeat the water over it for as long as he did not pour a residue. So if the doubt enters, and he has entered to be in another state, so let him continue in his Salaat, and there is nothing upon him; and if it is apparent, he should return and repeat the water over it; and if he sees it and with him is residue, he should wipe over it and repeat the Salaat, by the certainty; and if it was a doubt, so there is nothing upon him regarding his doubt, so let him continue to his Salaat’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan all from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

While taking Wudu’ if you are not certain of washing your forearm, you must go back to wash it and repeat all of the acts of Wudu’ that you doubt about its being washed or wiped which Allah has commanded to be done. This applies when you are still taking Wudu’, but when you complete Wudu’, stand up and move to another condition such as Salah (prayer) or something else, and then doubt about something which Allah, most High has mentioned or has made obligatory on you as part of Wudu’, then there is nothing necessary for you to do.

If during Wudu’ you doubt about wiping your head and you can find moisture in your beard, you must use such moisture to wipe your head and feet and if you do not find such moisture, you must not consider your Wudu’ invalid because of such doubt but you must proceed to your Salah (prayer). If you become certain that your Wudu’ is left incomplete, you must return to complete that which you are certain is left incomplete.’

Hammad has said that Hariz said that Zurarah has said, ‘I asked him (the Imam) about a man who has left out a certain part of his forearm or a certain part of his body for Ghusl (bath) because of sexual relation.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘If one doubts so and there is still moisture on him when he is in his Salah (prayer), he must wipe that part. If he becomes certain of a part being left incomplete, he must go back to complete it by pouring water on the part which is left dry and is without moisture. If one doubts while he has already assumed another condition, he must proceed to his Salah (prayer). There is nothing necessary for him to do about it. However, if it is discovered to have been left incomplete, he must go back to pour water on it; but if he finds moisture on it he only must wipe it and perform his Salah (prayer) again with certainty. If he has doubt about it there is nothing necessary for him to do because of such doubt and he must proceed to his Salah (prayer).”’
